title: Egress fallback & control-plane handshake patterns
content:
Purpose:
- Capture pragmatic patterns for (1) egress fallbacks across regions, (2) control-plane handshake semantics during partition/failover, and (3) service-mesh termination options when running mixed sidecar and sidecarless fleets.

Quick summary:
- Primary design is a layered fallback chain: local sidecar -> local edge proxy -> regional egress gateway -> global egress gateway. Each hop has an explicit policy envelope: allowed origins, TLS bindings, token-exchange hints, and circuit-breaker budgets.

Key constraints & goals:
- Keep latency SLOs for user-facing RPCs (p95 < 120ms) while preserving predictable throughput for model-serving north-south traffic.
- Avoid cascading control-plane stalls: data-plane should continue (with degraded policies) if control-plane is partially unavailable.
- mTLS must be end-to-end verifiable (auditable cert chain) for regulated customers; permit short-lived token exchange for ephemeral workloads.

Patterns and notes:
1) Handshake semantics (control-plane <-> data-plane):
   - Control-plane publishes policy bundles with sequence numbers (policy_v). Data-plane sidecars subscribe and ack at intervals.
   - If policy_v gap > 2 versions OR last_ack > 60s, sidecar switches to "frozen-policy" mode: allow only pre-approved egress lists and conservative retry limits.
   - Emergency policy: signed, timestamped minimal-allow list pushed via an out-of-band channel (S3-backed signed artifact) for long-lived partitions.

2) Egress fallback chain:
   - Preferred path: service -> local sidecar (mtls) -> local egress proxy -> regional gateway (mtls) -> destination.
   - Fallback 1: if sidecar unavailable, direct in-node policy agent enforces same policy but with higher token rate-limit.
   - Fallback 2: if regional gateway unhealthy, route to nearest healthy region via anycast DNS + connectivity hints (X-Region-Forward header) and apply regional egress ACLs.
   - Fallback 3: blackhole to control-plane-provided sink endpoint for telemetry while returning 503s with Retry-After for clients.

3) mTLS and termination options:
   - Sidecar-terminated mTLS (default): full visibility, per-pod identity certs (SPIFFE), automatic rotation.
   - Edge-terminated mTLS (for sidecarless workloads): edge proxy holds short-lived certs issued by control-plane CA; require JWT token binding for pod identity.
   - Pass-through: preserve end-to-end mTLS using TLS passthrough at egress gateways when destination requires original client cert. Only used for controlled partners.

4) Token exchange & billing headers:
   - Use token-exchange (OIDC token -> ephemeral service token) at the egress gateway for third-party API calls, with scope-limited tokens and TTL 5m.
   - Propagate X-Request-ID and X-Redwood-Region to help tracing and billing attribution.

5) Circuit breakers and resource budgeting:
   - Each hop enforces a budgeting token (budget-id header). On overload, gateway replies with 429 + Retry-After and routes a sample of requests to a "cold-path" with cheaper model variants.

Operational playbook (short):
- Deploy checklist: ensure CA rotation configured, policy bundle signing enabled, out-of-band artifact store reachable from all regions.
- Failure scenario: regional control-plane lost -> data-plane enters frozen-policy -> regional gateway marks unhealthy -> clients get p95 degradation but no data-plane stalls.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide TTL for frozen-policy mode (30m vs 4h).
- How to expose per-customer egress quotas in metrics (internal API vs prometheus labels).
- Evaluate cost of always issuing SPIFFE certs for ephemeral bursty dev workloads.

Links & references:
- Related: CONFLUENCE-4822 (control-plane policy model), JIRA-PLT-913 (egress gateway prototype).
- Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-proposals/pull/78

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc lightweight; move details to a canonical playbook if we converge.
- Reach out to SRE (Avery) for SLO impact analysis and to Applied ML (Samir) for cold-path model gating.
